title: Game of the Week Preview: Eye of the Republic Tigers on victory agianst Carthage Tigers - NewsBreak
text:
By Chris Pinson ,
1 hours ago
REPUBLIIC--The Repubic Tigers and Carthage Tigers will meet for the second consecutive postseason, and third time overall, when they collide in the Class 5 District 6 Semifinal, on Friday.
Dating back to last season, Carthage was able to overcome a 7-6 halftime deficit to knock Republic off in the District Championship game, at home. However, Repmo got revenge, this fall, by defeating Carthage during the regular season to lock up the No. 1 seed for the District Tournament.
Now, Republic enters round three coming off a much needed bye, while Carthage comes to town following their District Quarterfinal victory over Webb City. Even though the home field advantage and week off favor Republic, the orange and black Tigers aren't taking anything for granted.
"It's a really tough game, like it's always gonna be a four quarter game with them," said Republic senior, Keiran Govan. "It's fun to play Carthage, it always is."
"They're the same team as last year, basically, like, they have a lot of guys who returned and no matter who they put in the position, they're gonna be a great player and we know that we just have to stay locked in at all times. It's just awesome that we got the one seed. We've never done it here at Republic and we're really proud to be here and we just hope that everybody shows out and have a great game."
Whoever wins on Friday will advance to the District Championship and have the opportunity to play for a trip to the Class 5 State Quarterfinals. But even with that carrot dangling in front of them, Republic isn't looking that far ahead.
"We don't really wanna worry about the outcome as much because when you start worrying about the outcome that's when you're not locked in on the game," said Govan. "We're not gonna play fast, we're not gonna play physical when we're worried about winning or losing."
However, Govan and his teammates know they have the team to make a deep postseason run, but getting to the state championship game means running through an absolute gauntlet of a bracket.
"It's gonna be a tough game with everybody. Everybody who we've played it's a four quarter game. Neosho, whoever...when we get out of here, if we get out of here, you know, we know we'll play a great team, Helias and we just have to stay locked in."
